subject: SIG follow-up: clarifying RBAC exception & SCIM provisioning details
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-corp.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: temporary RBAC exception for migration window

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks for walking us through the SIG last week — a couple of follow-ups from our security review team. During our upcoming tenant migration (planned 2027-04-05), we need a temporary RBAC elevation for a small set of service accounts so the import process can write ownership metadata. To complete the SIG evidence set we need:  

- A mapping of Granted Roles -> API Scopes for the accounts in question (CSV or table).
- Confirmation of SCIM attribute mappings used for group membership and the deprovisioning TTL.
- The formal exception request form you use, signed/acknowledged, or guidance on the controls you will enforce if you approve the exception (timebox, monitoring, rollback).
- Clarification on MFA applicability for service accounts and how admin token issuance is audited.

Can you provide the RBAC mapping and SCIM attribute map by EOD Friday (2027-04-02)? We can treat the exception request as conditional on those artifacts.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jared
Security Engineer, Acme Corp

[Attachment requested: RBAC role mapping & SCIM attributes]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG follow-up: temporary RBAC exception for migration window

Team — forwarding Acme's asks. Quick plan:  

- Laura: can you generate the CSV that lists each role (internal name) -> granted permissions / API scopes + the exact account IDs they will use? Put it in the SIG folder.
- Karthik: please export the SCIM attribute map (group membership, externalId, active flag, email) and confirm the deprovision TTL. Acme asked for 1 hour; can we commit to that or document the observed delay?
- Hannah: we need a one-page mitigation summary we can include with the exception form: timeboxed (<=72 hrs), elevated logging (token audit, privileged call traces), and automatic rollback steps. Also include who will approve the exception internally.

Target: compile artifacts and draft exception form today so Laura can send to Acme tomorrow morning. If anything blocks, flag here.

— Marcus
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-corp.com>, Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: temporary RBAC exception for migration window

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the artifacts you requested and outlining our controls below. Attachments: SIG-RBAC-mapping.csv, SCIM-attribute-map.png, RBAC-exception-request-form.pdf (draft).

Short answers:  
- RBAC mapping: see attached CSV for the exact roles we will assign to the migration service accounts. Each row includes role_id, human_readable_name, api_scopes (comma-separated), and account_id.
- SCIM deprovisioning TTL: our SCIM pipeline attempts deprovision within 60 minutes; typical observed median is ~8 minutes for active deprovision events. We include the attribute set in the attached image (externalId, displayName, emails, groups, active).
- MFA: MFA enforcement is not applicable to non-human service accounts. Instead, we require short-lived tokens (rotated via our internal vault/STS) and we log token issuance and token-scoped administrative API calls.
- Auditing: all admin tokens issued during the exception window will have their issuance event and associated API calls recorded to our central audit stream and retained per our standard retention policy (90 days). We can provide an extract for the 72-hour window on request.

Proposed exception mechanics (draft in attached PDF):  
1) Timebox: up to 72 hours maximum.  
2) Access scope: strictly limited to the roles in SIG-RBAC-mapping.csv.
3) Monitoring: token issuance and privileged API calls are forwarded to your SIEM and ours (we will push syslog/forwarding details).
4) Rollback: role revocation script that will be run at end of window; confirmation posted to the ticket channel.
5) Internal approver: Marcus Lin (Director, Customer Security) + Hannah Schmitt (Security Ops).

Next steps: review the attachments and let us know if the deprovision SLA needs tightening. If these artifacts look good, sign the exception form and we will enable the roles on your migration account on 2027-04-05 at 02:00 UTC.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success — Security Programs
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: SIG-RBAC-mapping.csv (CSV), SCIM-attribute-map.png (image), RBAC-exception-request-form.pdf (PDF)]

From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-corp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: temporary RBAC exception for migration window

Laura — thanks for the artifacts, very helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before we sign:  

- You mentioned token issuance is logged and retained for 90 days. Can you confirm the log format and provide a 1-page sample extract showing the fields (timestamp, token_id, service_account_id, issuer, scope, action)?
- For SCIM deprovisioning: if a user is removed from AD during migration will the SCIM pipeline deprovision in <60 min *and* immediately revoke any active tokens for that user? We need assurance that tokens don't persist post-deprovision.
- If the exception is approved, can you confirm that it will be applied only to the explicit service_account_ids listed and that no other privilege creep will occur?

If you can provide the sample audit extract and confirm immediate token revocation on deprovision, we'll sign the form and proceed.

— Jared

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-corp.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: temporary RBAC exception for migration window — approvals and final notes

Jared — quick follow-up and confirmations from our side:  

- Sample audit extract: attached drive link contains a redacted example (fields: timestamp, token_id, service_account_id, issuer, scopes, api_call, status). We will export a matching JSON/CSV for the 72-hour window after the migration completes.
- Immediate revocation on deprovision: our SCIM worker triggers a revoke operation for active tokens when active=false is received from the IdP. In practice this revocation request is issued within seconds; the enforcement timing depends on token TTL but we rotate/shorten token lifetimes for the exception window to minimize exposure.
- Scope containment: the exception will be strictly limited to the service_account_ids in SIG-RBAC-mapping.csv. We will gate changes to the mapping via an internal PR + two approvers (Marcus + Hannah). Any deviation requires a new exception request.

Decision: Exception approved conditionally for 72 hours, pending your signature on the attached RBAC-exception-request-form.pdf. Controls will include elevated logging, token short-lifetimes for the window, daily verification reports posted to the Jira ticket, and automatic rollback.

Links: Drive artifacts — https://drive.google.com/open?id=1xY_example_drive_link; Ticket — https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/CLOUD-3124

Once you sign, we will enable the roles at the agreed time and provide the audit extract within 48 hours of completion.

Thanks — Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RBAC-exception-request-form.pdf (please countersign and return)]
